units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
What do you mean, sir?
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: During the Season, father, I only talk seriously on the first Tuesday in every month, from four to seven.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Well, make it Tuesday, sir, make it Tuesday.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: But it is after seven, father, and my doctor says I must not have any serious conversation after seven. It makes me talk in my sleep.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Talk in your sleep, sir? What does that matter? You are not married.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: No, father, I am not married.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Hum! That is what I have come to talk to you about, sir. You have got to get married, and at once. Why, when I was your age, sir, I had been an inconsolable widower for three months, and was already paying my addresses to your admirable mother. Damme, sir, it is your duty to get married. You can’t be always living for pleasure. Every man of position is married nowadays. Bachelors are not fashionable any more. They are a damaged lot. Too much is known about them. You must get a wife, sir. Look where your friend Robert Chiltern has got to by probity, hard work, and a sensible marriage with a good woman. Why don’t you imitate him, sir? Why don’t you take him for your model?
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: I think I shall, father.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: I wish you would, sir. Then I should be happy. At present I make your mother’s life miserable on your account. You are heartless, sir, quite heartless.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: I hope not, father.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: And it is high time for you to get married. You are thirty-four years of age, sir.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Yes, father, but I only admit to thirty-two—thirty-one and a half when I have a really good buttonhole. This buttonhole is not . . . trivial enough.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: I tell you you are thirty-four, sir. And there is a draught in your room, besides, which makes your conduct worse. Why did you tell me there was no draught, sir? I feel a draught, sir, I feel it distinctly.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: So do I, father. It is a dreadful draught. I will come and see you to-morrow, father. We can talk over anything you like. Let me help you on with your cloak, father.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: No, sir; I have called this evening for a definite purpose, and I am going to see it through at all costs to my health or yours. Put down my cloak, sir.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Certainly, father. But let us go into another room.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Rings bell .
There is a dreadful draught here.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Enter PHIPPS.
Phipps, is there a good fire in the smoking-room?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Yes, my lord.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: Come in there, father. Your sneezes are quite heartrending.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Well, sir, I suppose I have a right to sneeze when I choose?
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Apologetically .
Quite so, father. I was merely expressing sympathy.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Oh, damn sympathy. There is a great deal too much of that sort of thing going on nowadays.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: I quite agree with you, father. If there was less sympathy in the world there would be less trouble in the world.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Going towards the smoking-room .
That is a paradox, sir. I hate paradoxes.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: So do I, father. Everybody one meets is a paradox nowadays. It is a great bore. It makes society so obvious.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Turning round , and looking at his son beneath his bushy eyebrows .
Do you always really understand what you say, sir?
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: After some hesitation .
Yes, father, if I listen attentively.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Indignantly .
If you listen attentively! . . . Conceited young puppy!
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Goes off grumbling into the smoking-room .
PHIPPS enters .
Phipps, there is a lady coming to see me this evening on particular business. Show her into the drawing-room when she arrives. You understand?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Yes, my lord.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: It is a matter of the gravest importance, Phipps.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: I understand, my lord.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: No one else is to be admitted, under any circumstances.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: I understand, my lord.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: Bell rings .
Ah! that is probably the lady. I shall see her myself.
units.name: LORD GORING
